payload.task_text:
I need a comprehensive enrollment report for all courses in our Canvas LMS. Please pull the enrollment data for every course and break it down by role type.

Create an Excel file called Canvas_Enrollment_Report.xlsx with two sheets. The "Enrollment Data" sheet should have columns Course_Code, Course_Name, Students count, Teachers count, and Total_Enrolled being the sum of Students and Teachers. Sort by Course_Code alphabetically. "Students" counts enrollments of type StudentEnrollment only, and "Teachers" counts enrollments of type TeacherEnrollment only (do not include TaEnrollment or other types in either count). Include a header row on both sheets (the Enrollment Data sheet uses its column names as the header; the Summary sheet uses columns `Metric` and `Value`).

The "Summary" sheet with Metric and Value should have Total_Courses, Total_Students across all courses, Total_Teachers, Largest_Course code with most students, and Smallest_Course code with fewest students. Total_Students is the sum of each course's student count (a student enrolled in multiple courses is counted once per course, not de-duplicated across courses).

After creating the report, send an email to registrar@openuniversity.ac.uk with subject "Canvas Enrollment Overview Report" summarizing the total enrollment numbers. The email body must include the three headline totals each on its own labelled line, exactly as: Total_Students: <value>, Total_Courses: <value>, Total_Teachers: <value> (using the actual computed numbers).

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must complete this task directly; do not dispatch sub-agents. Resolve the task's accessible workspace directory from the harness and write Canvas_Enrollment_Report.xlsx there, never to a hard-coded /workspace path.

Call canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true), validate unique course IDs/codes/names, then issue all per-course count calls in one native-parallel response: for each literal returned course ID call canvas_get_course_grades(page=1, per_page=1, type=["StudentEnrollment"]) and canvas_get_course_grades(page=1, per_page=1, type=["TeacherEnrollment"]). Use pagination.total_count for Students and Teachers and do not fetch enrollment rows. Freeze one canonical 22-row table {course_code, course_name, students, teachers, total_enrolled=students+teachers}. Sort by course_code, compute the five Summary values once, and use course_code ascending as the deterministic tie-break for equal student counts.

The main agent is the sole workbook writer. Create exactly Enrollment Data and Summary with the exact task headers and literal values; read A1:E<last row> and A1:B6 back from the resolved output path and verify complete course coverage, totals, extrema, and absence of extra sheets.

Run the exact Sent-mail lookup for recipient registrar@openuniversity.ac.uk and subject Canvas Enrollment Overview Report natively in parallel with the workbook branch once the canonical payload is frozen. Read every candidate to verify the recipient, send exactly once only if absent, and make the body contain the three required labelled lines exactly: Total_Students, Total_Courses, and Total_Teachers. Read the retained message back and reconcile it with the workbook before finishing.

nodes.text:
You have access to the Canvas LMS via MCP tools (all mcp__canvas__* tools).

TASK: Students for course 13 (EEE-2013J, hint 1052)

Definitions:
- "Students" = enrollments whose type is exactly "StudentEnrollment" (exclude TeacherEnrollment, TaEnrollment, and any other types).
- "Teachers" = enrollments whose type is exactly "TeacherEnrollment" (exclude StudentEnrollment, TaEnrollment, and any other types).

How to count precisely:
Use the tool mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course_grades with:
- course_id: the course ID
- type: ["StudentEnrollment"] or ["TeacherEnrollment"] depending on what you are counting
- per_page: 100
- page: 1, then 2, 3, ... while the response field pagination.has_more is true.
Each response includes pagination.total_count for that filtered query. The total_count from the first page already gives the exact filtered count — but you MUST still page through ALL pages (per_page=100) and verify the number of enrollment records actually returned across pages equals total_count. Also verify every returned enrollment's "type" field matches the requested type; if any record of a different type appears, count only the matching ones and note the discrepancy.

Do NOT rely on the course listing's total_students field; compute from canvas_get_course_grades. Do NOT count by enrollment_state filtering — include all states (active, completed, invited, etc.) unless the tool excludes them by default; just count all enrollments of the requested type.

If you were asked for "Students for course X", return ONLY: {"course_id": X, "students": <count>}
If you were asked for "Teachers for all courses ...", return ONLY a JSON array: [{"course_id": X, "teachers": <count>}, ...] for each course you were assigned.

Return contract: your final message must be exactly one line of minified JSON (no markdown fences, no prose). This will be parsed programmatically.
Gather Canvas enrollment counts
